e-5470.knowledge_point: Calculating the Area of the Image of an Object Under a Linear Transformation Given a Diagram
e-5470.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14095768/assets/e8ff769df4089e6ed9a47d56d7317acf41b8aef6a255abc705c0e7ec31a446ea.png)

Consider the shaded region $D$ shown above. What is the area of the image of $D$ under the action of the linear transformation $\mathbf{T}$ with the standard matrix $T,$ given below?
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14095768/assets/c301e8b9a5cdc11007042c8a8d7bcddcfa5b1801bbf82e32c7f3ed08158440db.png)
e-5470.worked_solution:
Recall that for any linear transformation $\mathbf{T},$ we have the following connection between the area of $D$ and the area of the image $\mathbf{T}(D)$ under the action of $\mathbf{T}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\text{Area}(\mathbf{T}(D)) = |\det(T)| \cdot \text{Area}(D)
$$

From the diagram, we have

$$
\text{Area}(D) = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 3 \cdot 4 = 6.
$$

Computing the determinant of $T,$ we get 

$$
\det(T) = 4 \cdot 2 -  2 \cdot (-1) = 10.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(T(D)) & =|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D) \\  & =|\,10\,|\cdot 6 \\  & =60.\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that for any linear transformation $\mathbf{T},$ we have the following connection between the area of $D$ and the area of the image $\mathbf{T}(D)$ under the action of $\mathbf{T}\mathbin{:}$

$$

The unit square $D$ has vertices $(1,0),(0,0),(0,1),(1,1).$ What is the area of the image of $D$ under the action of the linear transformation $T$ with the standard matrix $T,$ given below?

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

$$
